title: Doctoral Research Symposium
pageTitle: 1st International Doctoral Research Symposium on Trustworthy AI and Intelligent IoT Systems (IDRS-TAIIS 2026)
intro: The International Conference on Trustworthy AI and Intelligent IoT Systems (TAIIS 2026) invites doctoral students to submit their ongoing research to the 1st International Doctoral Research Symposium on Trustworthy AI and Intelligent IoT Systems (IDRS-TAIIS 2026), to be held during December 3–5, 2026, at Asia University, Taichung, Taiwan.

The Doctoral Symposium will provide PhD students with an international forum to present their research, receive constructive feedback from experienced researchers, interact with other doctoral scholars, and establish valuable academic and professional collaborations.
objectives: Provide constructive feedback on ongoing doctoral research
Help students refine their research questions, methodology, and expected contributions
Facilitate interaction with senior researchers and industry experts
Encourage international research collaboration and networking
Support students in developing a clear roadmap for completing their doctoral research
topicsIntro: Submissions may address, but are not limited to:
topics: Internet of Things and Industrial IoT
AI for Healthcare and Smart Systems
Digital Forensics and Cyber Threat Intelligence

submissionCategories.title: Full Doctoral Symposium Paper
paragraphs: The paper should present a well-defined research problem, research gap, methodology, preliminary findings, expected contributions, and future research plan.

Accepted, registered, and presented papers may be submitted for consideration for publication in the planned Springer Lecture Notes in Electrical Engineering (LNEE) proceedings, subject to all conference and Springer Nature requirements.

submissionCategories.title: Doctoral Research Proposal/Poster
paragraphs: Suitable for doctoral students at an early stage who wish to present a research proposal, conceptual framework, or preliminary study.
These submissions will be included in the book having ISBN number but will not be considered for the Springer proceedings.

submissionRequirements: Background and motivation of the research
Research problem and identified research gap
Current research progress and future work
Specific areas on which the student would like to receive feedback
submissionRequirementsNote: The doctoral student should normally be the first author and must present the accepted work. Supervisors may be included as co-authors. Authors may also be requested to provide a brief letter or confirmation from their supervisor regarding their doctoral status and research progress.
reviewIntro: Submissions will be evaluated based on:
reviewCriteria: Relevance to the scope of TAIIS 2026
Originality and significance of the research
Clarity of the research problem and objectives
Potential academic, industrial, or societal impact
Overall quality and clarity of presentation
reviewNote: Acceptance will be based on peer review and the recommendations of the Doctoral Symposium Committee.
presentationIntro: Accepted doctoral students will be invited to:
presentationItems: Present their research during an interactive discussion or poster session
Receive feedback from an expert panel
Participate in mentoring and networking activities
presentationNote: Physical participation is encouraged. Online presentation may be permitted in exceptional circumstances, including visa, travel, financial, or medical difficulties, subject to prior approval by the Organizing Committee.
publicationParagraphs: Springer has accepted the TAIIS 2026 proceedings for planned publication in the Lecture Notes in Electrical Engineering (LNEE) series, which is indexed in Scopus and EI Compendex.

Peer-reviewed and selected full papers that are accepted, registered, and presented at the conference will be submitted to Springer for publication consideration. Springer Nature will conduct its own quality, integrity, formatting, and scope checks, and only papers that successfully pass these checks will be published.
Abstracts, extended abstracts, posters, and papers of fewer than four pages will not be considered for publication in the Springer proceedings.
awardsIntro: Subject to the recommendation of the Award Committee, the symposium may recognise outstanding contributions through:
awards: Audience Choice Award for Best Doctoral Paper
awardsNote: All registered and presenting doctoral participants will receive an official certificate of presentation or participation.

submissionProcedure: Authors should prepare their manuscripts using the prescribed conference/Springer format and submit them through the official TAIIS 2026 submission system. While submitting, authors should select the “Doctoral Symposium” track.

All submissions must be original, must not have been published previously, and must not be under review elsewhere. Authors must comply with the conference policies concerning plagiarism, research ethics, authorship, conflicts of interest, and the responsible use of artificial intelligence tools.
closing: Doctoral students from universities and research institutions worldwide are warmly invited to submit their research and participate in this valuable academic and mentoring opportunity.
cmtTrackNote: When completing your submission in Microsoft CMT, select the Doctoral Symposium track.
